articles.detail: 5 cycles, 5 completed, avg 8.6/cycle; selections were 11/10/11/14/9 against targets of 11/12/13/15/15; 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. The active experiment 2026-10-03-odds-in-future-block is not due until 2026-10-06; an interim reading was added to its entry (2 odds rows offered, 1 cited, and that one is correctly attributed and placed). No new experiment: today's two misses are one thin Saturday rather than a trend, and three more pipeline commits landed at 17:10-19:41 UTC on top of the 10-01 and 10-02 changes, so there is still no clean baseline to measure against.
weakestArea: Latin America is furthest from target at 0% against 5%, after 11-12% on the two previous days when the Brazilian election carried it; all seven AM datelines today are in the US. Science plus tech is 23% against 25% because politics took 25 of 43 articles and economy and tech both fell (economy 17 to 8, tech 13 to 5). The cause is supply: the selector reported a thin feed in all five cycles and stopped short of its target in four rather than pad.
watching: Hormuz: two tankers were struck and a fire was reported near an Aramco site; Polymarket traders put normal traffic by 31 December at 21%, down 7 points in a week.
Russia and Iran: Medvedev was in Tehran on defence cooperation, covered from state media alone.
Iran's space programme: launch plans announced by its space research centre, also state-media only.
Pakistan: two Islamabad datelines the day before the PTI long march planned for 4 October.
Ukraine: three Kyiv datelines in one day.
Germany: Unity Day marches against conscription and rearmament, sourced only from state or advocacy outlets.
Nigeria: four datelines (Uyo, Owerri, Makurdi, Maiduguri), all via Premium Times, which also carried a Geneva piece and is the day's top source at 5 of 43.
coverageGaps: Latin America has no dateline and Oceania has none; the region count fell from 6 to 5.
Tech was under its floor after dedup in four of five cycles (2, 1, 1 and 1 against 3) and economy in three (0, 2 and 1 against 3).

Science reached 5 for the day but was under its per-cycle floor in every cycle; the selector found the science feed to be mostly Scientific Reports manuscripts, with no Nature, Science, New Scientist, STAT, SciDev.Net or Carbon Brief item in the 18:00 cycle.

Science sourcing is weak: of the seven outlets behind the five science pieces, only Phys.org and The Guardian are science-capable; the rest are general outlets such as Business Standard, Free Malaysia Today and Express.
Politics is 58% of output (25 of 43), up from 41% yesterday.
One dateline is a country rather than a city (Netherlands); missingDateline does not count it.
Freshness was again measured on 2 of 43 articles, so the 0.5 median says little.
context: Volume fell to 43 from 59 with all five cycles completing in an average of 715s (selector 152s, writer 110s, editor 60s). The selector described roughly 40 niche entries per cycle, most of them opinion, sport, promoted posts or journal manuscripts, and 4-5 multi-source stories; the 22:00 cycle picked 9 against a target of 15. Multi-source met its target for the first time this week at 35% (15 of 43), partly because thin cycles shed single-source picks first, so it should not be read as a gain until it holds on a normal-volume day. If weekday feeds stay this thin, the science and tech RSS supply is the place to look, and the tuner may not edit RSS sources.
